newsitem.title: BELGIUM: All-party talks needed in Zaire - Belgium.
newsitem.headline: All-party talks needed in Zaire - Belgium.

text.p: Belgium urged all sides in the conflict in Zaire on Wednesday to seek a negotiated solution so the country could move towards fair and open elections and democratisation.

"We are calling on all parties to adopt a United Nations plan (which includes a ceasefire). Through negotiations all parties should be permitted to participate in the democratisation process," the foreign ministry said.

Asked at a weekly briefing whether Belgium regarded rebel leader Laurent Kabila as someone who could advance democracy in Zaire or backed Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, ministry spokesman Andre Querton said, "We stand for a policy, we do not back specific people."

On a two-day visit to Cairo, Foreign Minister Erik Derycke was quoted by Belgian agency Belga as saying Belgium was "ready to help with the restoration of Zaire" but on condition that the country return to peace.
"We hope for a speedy improvement in the situation and a return of refugees," Querton said,

In the meantime the ministry advised Belgians who had "no urgent reasons to stay in Zaire to reconsider their presence there." All Belgians travelling to Zaire should contact the Kinshasa embassy upon arrival.
There are currently 1,200 Belgians in the Zairean capital, 1,000 in Shaba and 700 in Lubumbashi.

Rebels in the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire on Wednesday rejected international pressure for a ceasefire and vowed to conduct a speedy war aimed at overthrowing ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.

The rebellion, which was launched in October, is moving closer to Mbuji-Mayi, diamond mining capital of the central Kasai region, and south into Shaba region which has some of the world's richest unexploited reserves of copper and cobalt.
Tens of thousands of Rwandan Hutus, who fled Rwanda after the 1994 massacres of Tutsis and moderate Hutus, are now fleeing before the advancing rebels, many of whom are Tutsis.
